source.title: A Behavioural and Representational Evaluation of Goal-Directedness in Language Model Agents
source.authors: Raghu Arghal; Fade Chen; Niall J. Dalton; E. Kortukov; Calum McNamara; A. Nalmpantis; Moksh Nirvaan; Gabriele Sarti; Mario Giulianelli

page_placements.theme: Decision-relevant state and policy across layers in chess and agentic models (state tracking, not shown look-ahead)

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses one-shot probes to decode future action sequences from model activations, a different method from the cited future-token studies. It also reports activation-patching results, though those interventions target grid-state information rather than a decoded plan.
record.gate_note: The one-shot plan-decoding results bear on future-action decodability and planning. The behavioral performance results, key/door results, and cited prior look-ahead findings do not measure the claim versions and are not rows. Activation-patching outcomes are recorded as related findings, but they do not directly test whether a precomputed future plan steers intermediate text.
record.test_reason: The study probes GPT-OSS-20B activations in a new setting, agentic grid-world navigation. A one-shot decoder reads multi-step future action sequences from pre- and post-reasoning activations and is compared with a 0.25^N random baseline. This bears on look-ahead beyond verse (V5) and on how far ahead plans reach (V6). The target is executed actions taken over later environment steps, decoded from three token activations. It is not text tokens from a single hidden state, so V2 is not directly tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that GPT-OSS-20B non-linearly encodes a coarse cognitive map and decodable multi-step action plans. Pre-reasoning activations keep longer-horizon plan structure, while post-reasoning activations favour next-action selection. They add that simple activation patching does not reliably alter behaviour, so causal links remain open.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses one-shot action-plan decoding from three activations and grid-state activation patching, rather than rhyme-word discovery or interventions that change a rhyme ending and measure intermediate text.
record.method_sensitivity: Decoder capacity and reasoning stage affect plan-decoding results: the 2-layer probe performs best overall; post-reasoning activations do better for short prefixes, while pre-reasoning activations do better for longer prefixes. Patching outcomes also depend on whether the intervention is confined to a single layer or applied across all layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-layer residual patching of grid-state or boundary tokens never changed the action (0/456). All-layer patching always did, and an unchanged-action control was stable (144/144).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this agentic navigation task, action-relevant state information is causally distributed across layers rather than localized in one tested layer.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The representational study uses one model and action trajectories in a controlled grid-world task. Plan decoding is a probe trained on executed actions, and longer-prefix exact-match accuracies are low. It does not intervene on the decoded future plans to test whether they steer generated intermediate text. Single-layer patching is negative, while the all-layer result has no run count stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 10 contains additional plotted prefix-accuracy curves, but exact values for most decoder, stage, and prefix combinations are not stated in the text and are not reliably recoverable from the supplied figure text. No relevant numerical rows were otherwise omitted.

untested.parts: No verse or rhyme task, and no frontier model of the V1 kind.
Not tested as stated. Decoding uses three token activations rather than a single hidden state, and targets environment actions rather than future text tokens.
No test of whether features are computed for the benefit of later positions rather than as a by-product of next-token prediction.
No rhyme task or attribution-graph method.
Only grid navigation with one model (GPT-OSS-20B) is tested; chess, Sokoban and other architectures are not. There is no causal test that a decoded plan steers later actions.

The study does not test whether decoded plans steer generation. It also does not rule out the probe deriving the path from decoded grid-state information, beyond an argument from decoder capacity. No heuristic or local-feature baseline is given.

missing.what: Prefix accuracies for N=2–4, for 4-layer decoders, and for post-reasoning at long prefixes. The text gives only qualitative descriptions: 2-layer post-reasoning strongest through N=4, with a crossover at N=5.

Trajectory-length decoding. Exact length match is 15.71% pre-reasoning and 18.85% post-reasoning, with median absolute error of 1 step. The authors cite this as evidence of coarse plans beyond the next action.

record.verdict_notes: V2 was removed from R5–R7 because the version specifies a single hidden state predicting future tokens. Here the decoder uses three chat-template token activations to predict actions executed over later environment steps. The random baseline 0.25^N is weak: a probe given decoded agent and goal positions could produce greedy paths, so above-chance long-prefix accuracy does not by itself separate a stored plan from grid-state information. The authors argue against this with the non-monotonic effect of decoder capacity. The study is not an original source for any version. Labelled peer-reviewed (ICML 2026 per the paper header).

versions.untested_parts: No rhyme or verse task, candidate rhyme-word representation, or intervention that changes an ending and tests intermediate text.
The study predicts future actions, not text tokens, from a set of three token activations rather than a single hidden state. It does not test arbitrary natural-language continuations.
No test of whether features are computed because they help later positions rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction.
No rhyme task or open attribution-graph/rhyme-probing method is used. The study evaluates GPT-OSS-20B in grid navigation.
The tested task is grid-world navigation with GPT-OSS-20B; chess, Sokoban, other architectures, and other task families are not tested.

The study tests decodability and probe-side autoregressive heuristics, not whether decoded plans causally steer generated intermediate text. It does not establish that the decoded plans are used in generation.

relationships.condition: GPT-OSS-20B grid navigation; 2-layer pre-reasoning decoder; prefixes of 5–7 actions
relationships.reason: Decodability falls steeply beyond about 4 steps (R5–R7 at 3.8–7.3%), consistent with mostly shallow plans. It stays far above 0.25^N, so a strict 'only a few steps' reading needs qualifying.
relationships.display_finding: Exact-prefix decoding accuracy fell to 3.8–7.3% for 5–7 actions, declining steeply beyond about 4 steps while remaining far above 0.25^N.

source_check.notes: Read the needed sections of arXiv v2, including the conclusion and App. F. The V6.suggested_status statement contains no study-specific assertion to verify; its cross-study counts were outside this check.

statements.correction: Pre-reasoning 2-layer exact-prefix accuracy: 7.3%, 5.0%, 3.8% at N=5,6,7; random baseline 0.25^N. Grid-state activation patching tested in §5.2 and App. F; decoded multi-step plans were not directly intervened on; their causal role remains unresolved.
statements.problem: The decoding values are correct, but the unqualified assertion that there is no causal test overlooks the activation-patching experiments.

statements.correction: 300 test trajectories; pre-reasoning 2-layer exact-prefix accuracy 7.3%, 5.0%, 3.8% at N=5,6,7; baseline 0.25^N. Authors interpret the results as recoverable longer-horizon structure. Grid-state patching performed; decoded-plan steering and a few-token planning ceiling not established.
statements.problem: Declining exact-prefix accuracy does not establish mostly shallow plans or a ceiling beyond four steps. The study does conduct grid-state steering, although it does not steer decoded plans.

statements.correction: One-shot decoding prevents conditioning later predictions on earlier decoded actions; decoder-capacity comparisons address decoder-side navigation. Grid-state patching performed. No control steering direction separating decoded plans from local next-token features is reported.
statements.problem: The missing plan-versus-local-feature steering control is correctly identified, but blanket claims of no heuristic control and no steering test are too broad.

statements.correction: Single-layer action changes: 0/456; unchanged-action control: 144/144. App. F reports all-layer patching always effective, without a run count; §5.2 specifies effectiveness at grid-state tokens or immediately before action output.
statements.problem: The counts match App. F, but the all-layer claim omits the main text's token-site restriction.
